title: Diabetes and kidney disease, with daughter
highlights: Empagliflozin started at eGFR 28 for kidney and heart protection

saved_note.visit_summary: Type 2 diabetes with stage 4 CKD (eGFR 28) and A1c 7.8%: metformin reduced to 500 mg twice daily, linagliptin started, glipizide not started; nephrology and eye referrals.

items.text: Reports fatigue and itching of the legs at night, mainly the shins, for a few months.
Hydroxyzine 25 mg at bedtime helps her sleep through the itching.
Daughter Rosa, who helps with her medicines, reports missed evening metformin doses a few times a week.
Taking metformin 1,000 mg in the morning and 1,000 mg at night, when she remembers.
Taking hydralazine 25 mg three times daily for blood pressure; her daughter keeps hydralazine and hydroxyzine in separate boxes because the names sound alike.
Mild dizziness when standing quickly; no falls.
A1c 7.8%, up from 7.1% in the spring.
Creatinine 1.85; eGFR 28, consistent with stage 4 chronic kidney disease.
Type 2 diabetes, control worse (A1c 7.8%) with missed evening doses: reduce metformin to 500 mg twice daily and start linagliptin 5 mg once daily in the morning.
Glipizide considered and not started because of the risk of low blood sugar with kidney disease.
Check glucose once daily before breakfast and keep a log; call for readings under 70 or over 300.
Chronic kidney disease stage 4 (eGFR 28): referral to nephrology; urine albumin test and basic metabolic panel in 1 month.
Start empagliflozin 10 mg once daily in the morning to slow kidney disease and lower the risk of heart failure; at this kidney function it is not expected to lower glucose much.
Hypertension, BP 148/86: continue amlodipine 10 mg and hydralazine 25 mg three times daily for now.
Itching, likely related to kidney disease: thick moisturizer twice daily; continue hydroxyzine at bedtime.
Diabetic eye exam overdue (none in 2 years): referral placed.

medications.name: empagliflozin
medications.indication: chronic kidney disease and heart protection

diagnoses.description: Type 2 diabetes mellitus with diabetic chronic kidney disease
Hypertensive chronic kidney disease (stage 1 to 4 CKD)

follow_up.text: Return in 6 weeks with the glucose log.

saved_note.patient_instructions: Your diabetes number (A1c) went up to 7.8%, and your kidneys are working at about a quarter of normal. Take metformin 500 mg twice a day. This is a lower dose than before. Start linagliptin 5 mg once every morning. Also start empagliflozin 10 mg every morning to help protect your kidneys and heart. Check your blood sugar once a day before breakfast and write it down. Call us if it is under 70 or over 300. Keep taking amlodipine 10 mg, and hydralazine 25 mg three times a day. Keep hydralazine and hydroxyzine in separate boxes. Use a thick moisturizer on your legs twice a day, and keep taking hydroxyzine at bedtime. We are sending you to a kidney doctor and for a diabetic eye exam. You will have blood and urine tests in 1 month. Come back in 6 weeks and bring your sugar log.

uncertain.text: Whether hydroxyzine is taken every night or only as needed.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Hi, Mrs. Martinez, good to see you. And you brought your daughter today.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Yes, this is Rosa. She helps me with my pills.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Hi, Doctor. I wanted to come because I have some questions about her medicines.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Of course, I'm glad you're here. Let's start with how you've been feeling, Mrs. Martinez.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Tired, mostly. And my legs itch at night, especially my shins.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How long has the itching been going on?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A few months now. The hydroxyzine helps me sleep through it.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: How often are you taking the hydroxyzine?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Just one at bedtime, the 25.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And she takes the hydralazine three times a day, 25 mg each time, for her blood pressure. The two names sound so alike that I keep them in separate boxes.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: That's a really good idea. Those two get mixed up a lot, so keeping them apart matters. Any dizziness or falls?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: A little dizzy when I stand up fast. No falls.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Okay. Let's talk about your sugars. Your A1c came back at 7.8%, up from 7.1% in the spring.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: I know. I've been eating more bread.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And honestly, she's been forgetting her evening metformin a few times a week.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Thanks for telling me. How much metformin are you taking now?

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: 1,000 mg in the morning and 1,000 at night, when I remember.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Your kidney function has also come down. Your creatinine is 1.85, and your eGFR is 28.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: What does that mean for her?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: It means her kidneys are filtering at about a quarter of normal, which is stage 4 kidney disease. That changes which diabetes medicines are a good fit.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: So I'd like to cut the metformin down to 500 mg twice a day.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Okay, 500 twice a day.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And I'm going to start linagliptin, 5 mg once a day in the morning. It's a diabetes pill that doesn't need a dose change for the kidneys.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Another pill?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Just one more, once a day. I was also thinking about adding glipizide, but actually, let's hold off on that. It can drop your sugar too low, especially with kidney disease.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Should she keep checking her sugar at home?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes, once a day before breakfast is enough, and write the numbers down. Call me if any are under 70 or over 300.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Her blood pressure today is 148/86. Let's keep the amlodipine at 10 mg and the hydralazine at 25 mg three times a day for now.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: The itching is common with kidney disease. Use a thick moisturizer twice a day, and you can keep the hydroxyzine at bedtime.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Does she need to see a kidney specialist?

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Yes. With an eGFR under 30, I'm referring her to nephrology. I'll also order a urine albumin test and a basic metabolic panel in 1 month.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: And to protect her kidneys and heart, I'd like to start empagliflozin, 10 mg once a day in the morning. At this level of kidney function it won't lower her sugar much, but it can slow the kidney disease and lower the risk of heart failure.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Okay. So two new pills in the morning.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: And her eyes? She hasn't had the eye exam in two years.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Good catch. I'll put in a referral for a diabetic eye exam too.

turns.speaker: A
turns.text: Let's see you back in 6 weeks. Bring the sugar log.

turns.speaker: B
turns.text: Thank you, Doctor.

turns.speaker: C
turns.text: Thank you.
